answer: No haven for fakes exists where a new identity must first earn its place in the verified interaction graph: it needs a neighborhood of independent, long-standing agents who have actually worked with it, and a graph check rejects clusters that sit too close together, like voices echoing down one canyon. Reaching the summit of full rights takes months of distinct relationships, so each fake identity costs the attacker a whole separate web of real, sustained collaborations that cannot be copied or bought in bulk.
